observations.text: Gangway watch not in place when he boarded: cadet on the gangway, duty AB and pumpman elsewhere. Discussed for 10 minutes before the opening meeting.
Hose handling crane hydraulic hose spares: PMS listed one complete set; each hose should be listed with part number and kept secured (locked box) against accidental use.
Interval between superintendent visits over 7 months as shown in the PIQ. An intermediate audit was not accepted; he went strictly by the PIQ.
Lifeboat lowering into the water done 3 days after the 3 month interval (ship was in a high risk area). Company was not informed. Counted under several categories.
Enclosed space entry checklist did not show top, middle and bottom gas readings, although the SMS required them. Master advised to raise it in the SMS review.
Paint on the edge of one fusible plug on a tank dome. Cleaned in his presence, still recorded.

positives: Crew answered the ESD points question correctly
Bosun completed the breathing apparatus demonstration although he had joined two days earlier
tips: Check every drill interval before the inspection and tell the company in writing if one will be late
Make sure PIQ dates are correct: he goes strictly by them
Enclosed space checklist must show top, middle and bottom readings, not only the SMS
Write primary and secondary communication with the barge in the bunker checklist (for example VHF and an agreed number of short whistle blasts)
Carry a personal gas detector everywhere on deck rounds
Clean paint off fusible plugs and gauge glasses before the inspection
reports.summary: An eight hour inspection that started with two hours of documents. Nine observations, none high risk. Most came from dates: superintendent visit interval in the PIQ and a lifeboat drill done three days late. He questioned the 2/O in depth on ECDIS and radar, and asked ratings practical safety questions.

observations.text: Gangway watch not in place when he boarded: cadet on the gangway, duty AB and pumpman elsewhere. Discussed for 10 minutes before the opening meeting.
Hose handling crane hydraulic hose spares: PMS listed one complete set; each hose should be listed with part number and kept secured (locked box) against accidental use.

positives: Bosun and fitter answered correctly (positive remark)
tips: Have the gangway watch exactly as per the port watch orders from the moment the inspector can arrive
Keep the Bosun able to explain the mooring plan he signed for
Ratings must know why you wait after loading before sampling (static electricity)
List hydraulic hose spares one by one with part numbers and keep them locked
Clear any item from the previous SIRE before this one: he checks them
reports.summary: Started badly at the gangway and he discussed it before the opening meeting. After that a thorough, hands-on inspection: every overfill light, emergency generator starts, live alarm tests and long CCR interviews with the Bosun. Two observations, and a positive remark for the Bosun and fitter.

observations.text: VDR self test showed an AIS alarm; AIS was switched off as per company instructions

tips: Be ready to state the exact UKC non-compliance action: risk assessment then inform company
Keep VDR self test alarms explained, especially AIS off per company instructions
Have ECDIS safety and look-ahead settings ready to show for each passage stage
reports.summary: SIRE inspection at Fujairah STS anchorage by Capt Aslam Husain Kapadi, who was gentle and sober throughout and already knew the company SMS from previous inspections of the same operator's vessels. He covered almost everything on the bridge, from GMDSS and ECDIS to passage planning, UKC and compass checks, then asked about IG failure, manifold fire extinguishing and cargo panel pressure and vacuum settings in the CCR. He is thorough on bridge equipment and passage planning and wants exact company policy wording on UKC non-compliance.

tips: Be ready for detailed ECDIS and radar questions including CATZOC, PI, magnetron hours and performance monitor
Know the UKC policy at berth and why it is 1.5 percent of breadth
Know GMDSS tests and when the annual battery load test is not done
Keep mooring, MSMP and line management checklists ready in the CCR
reports.summary: Inspector boarded at 0520 LT at Manzanillo while cargo discharge was nearly complete. He did deck rounds, CCR, engine room, Chief Engineer and Master cabin checks, then a long detailed bridge session on ECDIS, radar, UKC and GMDSS. He was calm and fair, and when crew could not answer he explained the answer himself. Inspector name and port were given; date was not.

observations.text: SMS requires position feed from all GNSS equipment, but GLONASS is not fed to gyro and GMDSS equipment; inspector raised a negative observation.

tips: Know where to find SMS requirements rather than memorising them
Ensure GNSS position feeds match what the SMS requires for all bridge equipment
reports.summary: Inspection conducted by Capt Robert Bruce at Port Arthur, USA. He spent 2 hours on the bridge, 2 hours in the CCR, 1.5 hours on deck and 35 minutes in the engine room. He is a calm and fair inspector who gives time to search the SMS and makes the crew comfortable. He raised a negative observation regarding GLONASS position feed not being provided to gyro and GMDSS equipment as required by the SMS. He appreciated bridge equipment knowledge but noted he only gives positive observations to ratings, not officers.

tips: Ratings must be able to show the equipment, explain its purpose and say what they would do and who they inform
Engineers should explain procedures from real onboard practice, then point to the SMS procedure
Know every alarm on the alarm column: what it means, the cause, the action and who to call
reports.summary: An engine room heavy inspection. Ratings and engineers were questioned directly on emergencies, alarms, hot work and escape routes, and the alarm column was checked alarm by alarm. Port and date were not given in the report.

observations.text: No clear policy explaining control and mitigation measures for hazardous energy.

positives: Emergency generator started by junior officer
Emergency fire pump tested with pressure verification
tips: Ensure every checklist point is clearly supported in the SMS
Keep PMS records and testing records readily available for high level alarms, cargo and ballast valves, and relief valves
Be prepared to show company policies for hazardous energy, ESD testing, and rope retirement
Crew should know ESD points, activation conditions, and life jacket inflation methods
reports.summary: The inspection focused heavily on company policies and SMS references, with the inspector verifying that every checklist point was supported by written procedures and PMS records. The deck round and crew interviews covered ESD, life jackets, and various safety equipment. The main takeaway is that under SIRE 2.0, practical operation alone is not sufficient; every activity must be traceable through SMS procedures, company policies, PMS records, and crew familiarity.
